To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transcription termination site of the malE operon in Escherichia colicorresponds exactly to the 3'end of the malG gene.
the 3'-end of the malEGF operon is localized 87 bp after the stop codons of malG, and that the malG gene is followed by two short open reading frames.
the malEFG and xylE genes are contiguous and that the malE operon is the longest one of the E. coli maltose regulon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the 3' part of the malE operon in Escherichia col.
the transcription of malEFG operons in the presence of xylose.
the transcription termination of malEFG operone and the 5' end of the xylEF gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the malEFG-xylE operon is transcribed from its promoter PmalE to the transcription termination site located 87 bp's beyond the stop codon malG.
the malEFG gene cluster of Eschericha coli is composed of 4 genes: malE, malFG, and malG, and that malG is the only gene of the cluster which is not transcribed as a monocistronic message.
xylE is a gene located after malG and is cotranscribed with the last two genes of the malE operon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the xylE and the malEFG genes are transcribed from the same promoter and terminated at the same site.
the malEFG and xylE genes form one operon.
the malEFG-xylEFG operon in E.c. is a 5,5 kb's DNA segment containing the genes coding for the maltose transport system, the xylose transport system and the xylose-protons symport.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we identified the transcription termination site of malEFG and we showed that orf1 corresponds to the 5'-part of the xyl gene.
the malEFG and the xylE genes belong to the same operon.
the malEFG and xylE genes are cotranscribed from the same promoter and that the xylE protein is the last protein coded by the malEFG-xylE operon.
